A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LatentR3 research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable, and corresponding material can be matched across the appendix reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original recommendation experiments on Toys, CDs, and Games, including component ablations, reasoning-length studies, popularity analyses, and training-time comparisons.

after.justification: V2 retains original experiments and adds Instruments results, explicit-reasoning comparisons, statistical testing, larger-model evaluation, and measured inference costs.

M1.justification: The multi-token procedure changes noise sampling from the first latent token in v1 Appendix E to the last token in v2 Appendix H. V2 also specifies initialization from a trained single-token model. The default architecture and two-stage training framework remain unchanged; LR-GRPO names the existing GRPO modification.

E1.justification: V2 adds Amazon Instruments to Toys, CDs, and Games, including accuracy and popularity evaluations. This extends coverage to another retail category while retaining the same next-item recommendation task.

E2.justification: V2 retains the existing baselines but adds untuned Base and zero-shot Rec-SAVER-style COT to Table 1. Appendix C and Table 5 additionally compare COT-RL against LatentR3. These additions substantially expand comparison coverage to explicit reasoning, which v1 excluded.

E3.justification: The reasoning-length sweep changes from {0,1,2,4,8} to {0,1,2}, alongside revised token sampling. New protocols include Qwen2.5-3B with LoRA, randomized generation for the statistical comparison, and inference timing on 100 examples per dataset using one A100, batch size 4, and beam sizes 10 versus 1 for COT. Existing dataset splits remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 substantially revises the reasoning-length sensitivity study, adds a grounding-versus-constrained-decoding analysis in Table 4, and directly measures inference efficiency in Appendix F. Popularity analysis expands to HR@10 and Instruments. The component-ablation experiments and values in Table 2 are retained.

E5.justification: V1 reports no repeated-run counts or formal significance tests. V2 Appendix D reports five randomized-generation runs and t-tests for BIGRec versus LatentR3 on CDs, with metric-specific p-values below 0.001. Appendix F reports averaging three timing measurements. This introduces statistical reporting, although its coverage is limited and training-seed variability is not established.

E6.justification: Existing three-dataset Table 1 scores and Table 2 remain identical, but new comparators, Instruments, Tables 4–7, and inference timing substantially expand the results. Existing popularity values also change: the Toys popular-item NDCG@10 improvement changes from 13.03% to 12.15%. Reasoning-length findings reverse under revised training, and the reported GRPO training-cost ratio changes from approximately 1/5 to 1/4.

T1.justification: In Section 3.2.2, v1 formally writes the batch-average baseline as an unnormalized sum despite describing an average. V2 adds division by the number of groups, correcting the mathematical definition to match that description. No substantial new theory or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: CoT-free latent reasoning, two-stage reinforcement learning, improved recommendation performance, and minimal inference overhead. Additional experiments support these claims without materially redefining them.

C2.justification: V1 interprets one token as optimal and longer reasoning as difficult to learn. V2 instead interprets its revised experiment as showing benefits from additional tokens with diminishing returns, and removes the longer-sequence limitation from the conclusion. Appendix C also adds an explanation of COT-RL failure involving difficult sampling, formatting requirements, and reward gains disconnected from recommendation accuracy.

D1.justification: V2 newly discloses constrained decoding for BIGRec, timing settings, and multi-token initialization details. It replaces the anonymous code link with a named GitHub repository and describes available reproduction scripts. The main optimizer and learning-rate disclosures are retained; the decoding disclosure alone does not establish a change to the earlier implementation.

R1.justification: V2 adds R2ec by You et al. (2025) to Section 5 and the references. The broader positioning against explicit CoT supervision and existing latent-reasoning methods remains stable. ReasoningRec and DeepSeek-R1 publication updates concern already cited works.

P1.justification: V2 edits introductory and methodological explanations, introduces the LR-GRPO name, merges the baseline and implementation appendices, and adds ethics, reproducibility, and LLM-use statements. The main section sequence and much of the existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a different document template and extensively redraws the figures. Figure 4 changes its performance panel from bars to a radar chart; popularity and reasoning-length displays gain panels and revised axes. Table 1 expands, Tables 4–7 and an inference-time figure are added, and appendix displays are reorganized.

improvement.justification: The added explicit-reasoning comparisons and measured inference costs strengthen arguments that v1 supported less directly. However, significance evidence covers only randomized generation on CDs against BIGRec, the length sweep drops four- and eight-token tests, and new Instruments entries contain apparent metric inconsistencies: BIGRec N@5 is 0.0938 while H@5 is 0.0807. These limitations temper the additional evidence, supporting a limited net improvement.
